messages.content:
For breakfast I had a 12 ounce iced coffee and a banana.

For lunch I had a quesadilla

Breakfast four ounces of asparagus, two eggs, one piece of gluten free bread.

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

message.reasoning:

They want us to log foods. They mention breakfast items: 12 oz iced coffee, banana, 4 oz asparagus, 2 eggs, 1 piece gluten free bread. Lunch: quesadilla. We need to call log_food for each item. But we have no portion amounts for banana, quesadilla, eggs? We can assume typical portion sizes: banana maybe 1 piece, eggs 2 pieces, gluten free bread 1 piece, quesadilla maybe 1 piece? But we need portion_amount and portion_unit. For banana: 1 piece. For eggs: 2 pieces. For bread: 1 piece. For quesadilla: 1 piece. For iced coffee: 12 ounces. Asparagus: 4 ounces. So we will call log_food for each. Use default unit grams if not specified. But we can specify unit. We'll use "ounces" for iced coffee and asparagus. For banana, eggs, bread, quesadilla: "pieces". Provide meal_name accordingly: breakfast for all breakfast items, lunch for quesadilla. Let's do separate calls.
